transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I came in because… you know, over at the domino table, those men, they say things that aren’t just regular talk. Little messages, like they’re meant for me. And sometimes the radio announcer too, he’ll say something and I know it’s a warning for me to be careful.

My wife says, “Oh, that’s just talk,” but she don’t sit there and hear it the way I do. Dominoes used to be simple, you know, just counting and passing the time… but now I can tell when they’re trying to tell me something. So I figured I better come in.
Do you think these messages are meant for you alone, or could others understand them as well?

I think they’re meant for me, doctor. Other folks might hear the words, sure, like my wife says it’s just regular talk, but they don’t catch what it’s pointing to. Like at the domino table, a man lays a tile down and says something about “watch yourself,” and maybe he’s talking about the game, but I know it’s a warning.

Same with the radio announcer sometimes… I’ll be sitting there, and he says a little thing in that certain way. My wife, she’ll be in the kitchen fussing with the coffee, says I’m making too much of it. But she don’t hear it how I hear it. It’s for me to be careful.
Do these messages and warnings you're hearing seem to be part of a larger plan or story, or are they more random and unrelated to each other?

Well… I don’t know if I’d call it a whole story, doctor. It’s more like little warnings, here and there. The men at the domino table, they’ll say something, and the radio man too sometimes, and I know it’s meant for me to be careful.

My wife says it’s just talk, but she says that about a lot of things… like when I tell her the coffee’s too strong, she just laughs. But no, these messages, they feel connected in that they’re pointing at me. Like they’re trying to tell me, “watch yourself.”
Do you ever find it hard to explain what you're trying to say, or that your thoughts get jumbled up?

Yes, doctor, that happens. I start trying to explain one thing and my mind runs off on me… like I’ll be thinking about the church choir, then all of a sudden baseball comes in, then I remember some repair I meant to do, then my friend’s name pops up, and before I know it I’m back at the choir again.

It goes so fast I can’t hold the one thought long enough to say it right. I know what I mean at first, but then it gets all tangled, and folks look at me like I wandered off the road.
Have you been hearing these messages for a short period or has it been going on for a while?

It’s been going on a while, doctor… not just a week or two. I’d say on and off maybe nine months now.

Sometimes it’ll be quiet for a bit, and I think, well, maybe that’s done with, then something on the radio or somebody talking will come through that certain way again. Nine months, around there… hard to pin it exact, like remembering when I last fixed the screen door, but it’s been most of the year, I think.
Do you think all these messages and warnings are connected, like they're all part of something bigger that's going on?

Yes… yes, doctor, I think they’re connected some way. Not like a movie story, maybe, but the men at the domino table, and then sometimes that radio announcer, they’ll say these little things that land right on me.

My wife says, “That’s just talk,” but she says that about plenty, you know… she’ll wave her hand like when I ask where she put the good towel. But I know those messages are meant for me. They’re warnings, like telling me to be careful.
Do you find it hard to keep your thoughts in order when you're trying to think about these messages?

Yes, doctor… it gets hard to keep them straight. I’ll start thinking on the message, trying to figure what it means, and then my mind jumps—like from the choir, then baseball somehow, then that repair I was supposed to do, then my friend’s name comes in, and before I know it I’m back at the choir again.

It’s so quick I can’t hold one thought long enough to explain it right. I try to line it up, but it runs off on me.
Have these messages and warnings been causing problems for you at home or with your relationships?

Yes… it has, I suppose. My wife don’t like when I get to talking about it, says I’m making the house uneasy. And I’ve missed choir rehearsal some, which I never liked doing, because I been with them folks a long time… though the new hymnals, the print’s too small anyway.

And the garden, too—I let parts of it go. Tomatoes don’t wait on a man, you know. You miss a few days and the weeds think they own the place. The domino games… well, I don’t sit in like I used to. I think I made the table uncomfortable, asking what they meant by certain things, and then it gets quiet. So I just stay away more now.
Do you find that your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow when you're talking about these messages?

Yes, sir… they do get hard to follow. I’ll be talking about the message and then my mind runs off—choir, then baseball, then some repair I got to do, then an old friend of mine, and right back around again.

It goes so fast I can’t hold it still long enough to say it plain. Like I know what I mean, but by the time I start explaining, it’s already moved on somewhere else.
When your thoughts jump from one thing to another, do they still make sense to you, or do they feel completely disconnected?

Well… while it’s happening, it sort of makes sense to me, I think. Like I can see the road from one thing to the next, but if I try to tell it out loud, it sounds all broken up.

My mind runs from the choir to baseball, then to a repair I meant to do, then my friend’s name pops in, and back again… so fast I can’t hold one thought long enough to explain it right. It ain’t like blank nothing, it’s more like everything is chasing everything else.
When you have these thoughts, do you feel like they're coming from your own mind?

I… I don’t rightly know how to answer that. They feel like my thoughts in one way, because they’re in my head, you know. But then I get to wondering where a thought starts from, and that’s like trying to find the first weed in the garden.

Sometimes I’ll be sitting there and one comes along, and I say, “Well, that’s mine,” but then I get distracted thinking about whether I left the shed door open, or if my wife moved the mail again. So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really pinned it down like that.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being controlled by something or someone outside of yourself?

I don’t know if I’d say controlled, doctor. That sounds… like a strong word. I haven’t really noticed it that way.

Sometimes my thoughts just get to running, like when you pull one string and the whole pile comes with it. But controlled by somebody? I’m not sure. I’d have to think on what you mean by that. I know when the radio used to skip in the truck, my wife would say it was the antenna, and I’d say no, it’s the road bumps—but that’s different.

So… no, I can’t rightly say someone outside me is controlling them.
Do you think there's a main idea or theme behind all these messages you're hearing?

Yes… I think there is, doctor. It’s like they’re telling me to be careful. The men at the domino table, they’ll say something ordinary, I guess, but the way they say it… it feels meant for me.

And the radio too, sometimes the announcer says a thing and I know it’s not just talk. My wife says, “That’s just the radio,” but she didn’t hear it the way I did. It’s like a warning. Not always loud or plain, more like… little messages tucked in there.
Do you think all these messages and warnings are part of a single, larger plan or idea that's being communicated to you?

Well… yes, I think so, doctor. Maybe not a plan like somebody wrote it down on paper, but it feels connected.

That’s why I came in, really. The men at the domino table, they’ll say little things, and the radio announcer too sometimes, and it feels meant for me. My wife says it’s just talk, just folks talking or the radio doing what it does, but I know there’s a warning in it. Like they’re telling me to be careful.

Now, I don’t always know careful of what. That’s the part that gets me turned around. Like when you see storm clouds but don’t know if it’ll pass over or hit the house. But it feels like it’s all pointing the same way.
Do you often find yourself having trouble expressing your thoughts in a way that makes sense to others?

Yes, sir… sometimes I do. It’s not that I don’t know what I mean at first, but my mind gets to running too fast.

I’ll start trying to tell my wife one thing, and then I’m thinking about the choir, then baseball, then something needing fixing at the house, then my old friend, and somehow I’m back where I started. It goes so quick I can’t hold the one thought still long enough to explain it right.

Folks look at me like, “What are you talking about?” and I know I’ve wandered off, but it’s hard to stop it once it starts.
Do you feel like these thoughts about the messages are your own thoughts, or do they feel like they're coming from somewhere else?

I’m not sure how to answer that plain, doctor. They feel like my thoughts because they’re in my head, you know… I’m the one thinking on them.

But then sometimes it’s like they get stirred up by what somebody says, like a word on the radio or one of those men talking, and then my mind runs with it. Makes me wonder if I’m putting it together myself or if there’s something else to it.

It’s hard to tell. Like when you hear a bird at night and you think, now why is that bird calling then… my brother used to say that meant weather was changing, but I don’t know if that’s true. Same kind of feeling, I guess. I just don’t know for sure where it starts.
Do these thoughts about the messages ever feel like they're forcing their way into your mind without you wanting them to?

I don’t rightly know, doctor. I can’t say they force in like somebody shoving through a door. It’s more… I hear something, or remember something, and then my mind starts chewing on it.

Like when a tune gets stuck in your head after Sunday service—you don’t ask for it exactly, but there it is. My wife’ll be humming while she cooks, and then I’m thinking about that hymn all afternoon, and then somehow I’m thinking about what the announcer said, and whether it meant something.

So… I don’t know if that’s forcing or just me not being able to let it go. It bothers me some, but I can’t put a clean name on it.
Do you think your mind jumps between thoughts because of what you're hearing from others, like the radio or the men at the domino table, or is it more because of your own thoughts and worries?

I think it’s more my own mind running, doctor… though things I hear can set it off. Like somebody says something at the domino table, or the radio’s on, and then I’m off thinking about that.

But it don’t stay there. It jumps—choir, then baseball, then something needing fixing at the house, then an old friend of mine, and back around again. It goes so fast I can’t hold one thought still long enough to say it right.

My wife will ask me what I mean, and by then I’ve already gone three roads away from where I started.
When your thoughts jump from one thing to another, do they still seem to make sense to you in a strange way, or do they feel completely disconnected and nonsensical?

It makes sense to me while it’s happening, I think… not like nonsense words or anything. It’s just too fast.

My mind’ll go from the choir to baseball, then I’m thinking about something that needs fixing at the house, then an old friend of mine, and before I can explain that, I’m back around somewhere else. Like taking too many turns on little roads.

So it ain’t completely disconnected to me, but I can’t hold one thought long enough to say it right.
Do you think all these messages and warnings are part of a single story or idea that's being communicated to you?

I don’t know if I’d call it one whole story, doctor… but it feels connected, yes. Like the men at the domino table will say a thing, just casual-like, and then later the radio announcer says something that sounds like it’s pointing the same way.

My wife says, “That’s just talk, don’t pay it mind,” but I can’t shake it. It feels like little warnings meant for me, telling me to be careful. Not always plain, not like somebody writing me a letter, but… there’s a thread to it.

Like when you’re patching a fence, one board don’t look like much, but then you step back and see where it’s leaning. That’s how it feels to me sometimes.

I think it’s more my own mind running, doctor… though things I hear can set it off. Like somebody says something at the domino table, or the radio’s on, and then I’m off thinking about that.

But it don’t stay there. It jumps—choir, then baseball, then something needing fixing at the house, then an old friend of mine, and back around again. It goes so fast I can’t hold one thought still long enough to say it right.

My wife will ask me what I mean, and by then I’ve already gone three roads away from where I started.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thought disorder is organized or disorganized
doctor.question: When your thoughts jump from one thing to another, do they still seem to make sense to you in a strange way, or do they feel completely disconnected and nonsensical?

target_item.name: Racing_Thoughts
target_item.manifestation: My mind runs from the choir to baseball to repairs to my friend and back again so fast that I cannot hold one thought long enough to explain it right.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient's thoughts jumping from one topic to another feel connected or nonsensical, which most directly concerns flight of ideas/racing thoughts.

patient.answer:
It makes sense to me while it’s happening, I think… not like nonsense words or anything. It’s just too fast.

My mind’ll go from the choir to baseball, then I’m thinking about something that needs fixing at the house, then an old friend of mine, and before I can explain that, I’m back around somewhere else. Like taking too many turns on little roads.

So it ain’t completely disconnected to me, but I can’t hold one thought long enough to say it right.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of a coherent delusional system
doctor.question: Do you think all these messages and warnings are part of a single story or idea that's being communicated to you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: Doctor, I came because the men at the domino table and sometimes the radio announcer give little messages meant for me, and even when my wife says it is just talk, I know they are warning me to be careful.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the perceived messages and warnings form a coherent communicated idea, which directly relates to the patient's fixed belief that radio announcers and men at the domino table send messages meant for him.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d call it one whole story, doctor… but it feels connected, yes. Like the men at the domino table will say a thing, just casual-like, and then later the radio announcer says something that sounds like it’s pointing the same way.

My wife says, “That’s just talk, don’t pay it mind,” but I can’t shake it. It feels like little warnings meant for me, telling me to be careful. Not always plain, not like somebody writing me a letter, but… there’s a thread to it.

Like when you’re patching a fence, one board don’t look like much, but then you step back and see where it’s leaning. That’s how it feels to me sometimes.
